answer: A per-subnet token-bucket limiter caps each agent's voyage through the economy, forcing every new identity to queue at the same narrow jetty of connection quotas before any transaction clears. Because each sybil must independently burn scarce handshake tokens and isolated server resources, the comet of forged identities stalls under per-subnet throttling instead of scaling. Colluding clusters incur an exponential slashing penalty bounded by O(Delta * S).
